ladder.label: Groundwork
ladder.means: Tools, formats and loaders; the game's own executable has not been run yet.

ladder.label: Executable runs
ladder.means: The game's code starts: its entry point runs and its imports are answered.

ladder.label: Graphics device
ladder.means: It creates its graphics device, queues and command lists, but nothing reaches the screen.

ladder.label: First frame
ladder.means: Frames reach the screen, even blank or garbled ones.

ladder.label: Menus
ladder.means: The game's own screens are drawn: first-boot screens, menus or the intro video.

ladder.label: World loads
ladder.means: It loads into the game world, though the picture may still be dark or incomplete.

ladder.label: In-game
ladder.means: Player control in the world, with a recognisable picture.

ladder.label: Playable
ladder.means: In-game for 30 minutes or more without a crash, at 20 frames a second or better.

compat-layer.label: Compatibility layer
compat-layer.about: Runs the console executable's x86-64 code directly on the PC and supplies the console's system libraries and graphics API underneath it, translating the GPU programs on the way.

recompiler.label: Recompiler
recompiler.about: Translates the console executable, or the parts of it that differ, into a new PC program ahead of time.

emulator.label: Emulator
emulator.about: Emulates the console's hardware or operating system broadly, not only the interfaces this game calls.

boot-harness.label: Boot harness
boot-harness.about: A focused harness that boots this one game to test parts of the pipeline, with stand-ins where the rest is missing.

fork.label: Fork
fork.about: Builds on another tracked project, adding its own fixes or changes the original has not merged.

other.label: Other route
other.about: A different way to the PC, for example through another console's build.

projects.name: Victory
projects.summary: Boots through the first-boot screens, intro video and start screen at 30 fps and loads into the first mission. In the world only the title card shows; the scene stays dark and frames take 0.5 to 1.8 s.
projects.evidence: README status table dated 2026-11-23, one machine, RX 6700 XT
projects.caveat: entering the world can hang a real GPU; single test machine

projects.name: AnyXboxX
projects.summary: Through its integration of Victory plus community patches, the game passes its menus at 30 fps and reaches the opening cutscene of the first mission with no GPU hang over 5 minutes. The 3D scene is black and the world runs at 0.3 to 0.5 fps.
projects.evidence: README status box dated 2026-11-24, i7-13700KF + RTX 4070 SUPER
projects.caveat: game path runs on a fork of Victory; the project's own emulator core has not run the game

projects.name: Project Asteria
projects.summary: The maintainer reports that a local development build reaches the menus and allows settings changes. Output stays black when entering the 3D scene.
projects.caveat: Public branch reproduction, hardware, timings and distinct fork implementation not yet independently verified; upstream results are not counted

projects.name: Palmwave
projects.summary: Presents the first screens and intro video at 30 fps, then loads the world behind loading screens. After that it shows nothing while it compiles the world's compute pipelines, though runs of up to 60 minutes did not crash.
projects.caveat: needs a patched executable (hang detector disabled); claims the world loads but no world picture is presented, so rated menus

projects.name: Five Star Recomp
projects.summary: Loads the executable with all imports resolved and shows its logo, intro video, first-run screens and menus with full UI text. Loading story mode starts but stops on corrupted game memory.
projects.evidence: README status table, details in project wiki
projects.caveat: first-run screens driven by a scripted gamepad

projects.name: OpenScarlett (Community Edition)
projects.summary: Runs the first-boot settings, legal screens and start screen at a steady 30 fps and plays the 4K intro movie with sound. It stops while streaming the scene behind the menus, before the menus themselves.
projects.caveat: title not named (described as a newer retail game); building needs the user's own GDK with Xbox extensions

projects.name: XCL
projects.summary: Starts in about 4 s and runs at a steady 30 fps through its menus into the settings screen without crashing. Gameplay is not reached and some mesh pipelines are refused.
projects.evidence: README games table and highlights (26,503-record shader pack)
projects.caveat: title not named; identified by its shader pack size

projects.name: Xbox2Windows
projects.summary: A modified diagnostic build of the executable played the intro, showed readable setup text and reached loading. Startup of the unmodified executable, menu navigation and gameplay are not verified.
projects.evidence: README startup note, RTX 4060 Laptop (plus an RX 9070 XT report)
projects.caveat: needs a patched diagnostic executable that continues past assertions; title not named

projects.name: TuxBox
projects.summary: On Linux under stock Proton Experimental the game shows its player selection prompt at 4K. The Series S mode stops on a texture allocation before presenting, and the Windows backend is not yet running games.
projects.evidence: README, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER on Linux
projects.caveat: Linux/Proton only; progress beyond the first prompt not described

projects.name: BootTest
projects.summary: A debugger harness with stand-in DLLs boots the game, streams its archives, runs the frame loop and draws the start-screen prompt bar through translated shaders on a PC GPU. Screens after that go black again; compute and tiled textures are not done.
projects.caveat: runs under a debugger harness that skips assertions; only the first UI element drawn

projects.name: OpenScarlett
projects.summary: An unnamed retail title clears 36 boot stops and presents over 360 4K frames without crashing, with its first-frame clear and texture draws executing on the GPU. Visible scene output is listed as the next step.
projects.caveat: title not named (retail GRDK 2504/2510 build); no picture content described

projects.name: Holy Interoperability
projects.summary: A retail title creates its window, device and translated pipelines, streams start-up data and presents its first frame about 30 s in. It then stops in its own start-up code because its movie player uses pipelines that do not exist yet; nothing drawn has been seen.
projects.caveat: title not named by policy (a reference title); may not be this game

projects.name: Leonida
projects.summary: Community continuation of the original project, which went private on 23 November. Its retail boot creates the graphics device, five command queues, fences and hundreds of command lists, then stops at the first descriptor heap; no frame yet. All 26,503 shaders translate to SPIR-V that validates.
projects.evidence: Boot chain notes in the repository, one machine; translator corpus runs
projects.caveat: README itself still says the game does not boot; boot progress comes from verified project notes
projects.tested_on: Windows; translator GPU tests on 30+ GPU/driver combinations

projects.name: Kajcsi Recomp
projects.summary: The loader, hook engine and import policy work and the game's side DLLs initialize under it, but the main executable has not been run. First frame and title screen are not started.

projects.name: Xbox Emulator
projects.summary: Runs several other Xbox Series titles, but has not run this game because its dump lacks the executable. Only the shader package was examined, with about a third of sampled vertex shaders translating.
projects.caveat: no executable available to the project

projects.name: PercyScarlett
projects.summary: Runs another retail Series title in-world; for this game one status row claims the account picker, intro video and setup screens render. The same README says to add the package and wait for the executable, so a real run is not clearly shown.
projects.evidence: README status table row and readiness section
projects.caveat: title only hinted at; self-contradictory, no screenshots for this game; rated lower

projects.name: ScarlettX
projects.summary: A Series HLE layer that runs two smaller retail titles; it has no console shader translation yet and reports nothing on this game.

projects.name: scarlett-layer
projects.summary: Experimental layer whose only retail result is another title's menus; no work on this game is reported.

projects.name: XValkyrie
projects.summary: Translation layer for Xbox One and Series titles with dozens of other games tried; this game is not among the titles listed in its README.
projects.caveat: full compatibility list (COMPATIBILITY.md) not on disk

projects.name: AnyPS5
projects.summary: A relinker that ports PlayStation 5 executables to PC; it does not target Xbox builds and reports nothing on this game.
